summary:
LUNARIS: Smarter Lunar Landing Site Selection

LUNARIS is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to help mission planners identify and compare potential lunar landing sites. Through an immersive 3D Moon environment, users can select up to three candidate locations and evaluate sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and communication opportunities. The platform provides side-by-side site comparisons, a guided landing-site selection workflow, and a cinematic 3D spacecraft landing simulation.

LUNARIS addresses the challenge of planning lunar surface missions by bringing critical environmental and communication considerations into one intuitive experience. It helps users understand the trade-offs between candidate landing locations before selecting a preferred site.

This project is important because reliable sunlight and communication are essential considerations for sustained lunar exploration. By making complex mission-planning concepts interactive and accessible, LUNARIS supports better-informed decisions and helps inspire the next generation of lunar exploration.
details:
About LUNARIS
We developed LUNARIS to make lunar landing site planning easier to understand and explore. Instead of looking at separate maps, data, and scientific measurements, users can explore the Moon in an interactive 3D environment and compare potential landing locations in one place.
Users can select up to three candidate sites, then evaluate each location based on sunlight availability and whether Earth is visible for potential communication. They can compare the results, choose a preferred landing site, and watch a 3D simulation of a spacecraft descending to the lunar surface. The experience ends with a mission summary.
One of the main benefits is that it brings several important mission-planning considerations together in a way that is easier to explore, even for people without a background in space science. It also helps users see that choosing a landing site is not simply about finding a flat or convenient location. Sunlight, terrain, and communication opportunities all matter.
We built the project using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Tailwind CSS. We also incorporated NASA JPL Horizons data for lunar trajectory information, alongside our own astronomy calculations and terrain-based reference approximations.
Creativity was a big part of our approach. We wanted the project to feel like an actual mission-planning experience rather than a traditional data dashboard. The interactive Moon, guided workflow, site comparisons, and landing simulation were designed to make the process more engaging.
Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, usability, performance, and transparency. We made a point of distinguishing live astronomical data from calculated estimates and simplified terrain references, rather than presenting every result as precise NASA measurement.
Our goal is to help people better understand the challenges of lunar exploration and show how interactive technology can support the decisions involved in planning future missions.
